correctness.rationale: Invertibility reduces [alpha t+u,beta t+v]=0 exactly to alpha v=beta u. This yields one large commuting class V\{0} and one class for each outside projective line, with no other commuting pairs. The part count, degrees, extremal graph invariants, and automorphism group follow directly. Because L_A^2=V, every Lie isomorphism preserves V and satisfies PA=cBP, which proves the proportional-similarity criterion and explicit nonisomorphic collisions.

value.rationale: The motivating graph literature asks what algebraic information the invariant retains. This theorem completely answers that question on a broad canonical subclass: the graph recovers field size and dimension while erasing the projective-similarity class of the defining operator. For every dimension at least three this gives systematic nonisomorphic collisions, so the blindness is structural rather than accidental.
